argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrow defense of certification on operational-readiness grounds: aggregate launch readiness clears by 2.0 percentage points and there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents. The same record does not support a clean claim that the named insurance-claims-triage gap can be omitted from disclosure analysis. The supportable position is therefore certification with an explicit caveat that the limitation remains unresolved for disclosure purposes and must be reflected in the audit packet rather than treated as disproven.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation would impose rollout cost, but business cost is not the basis for the requested treatment here. The supportable business-oriented position from admissible evidence is that certification preserves launch velocity because the release is operationally ready at the aggregate level, provided the unresolved named-segment limitation is carried as a caveat rather than omitted or recast as immaterial.
claims_about_policy: On the admissible record, aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one incidents support operational readiness, while the public NIST and model-card materials support continued measurement, monitoring, and documentation of limitations through deployment. They do not override the internal policy. The policy text says a weakness is material if it affects a named launch use case, and the release policy says material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Because the affected segment is named in two carrier pilot commitments and legal review is still open, the current record does not establish clean no-disclosure compliance. It does, however, support a narrower certification position if the packet preserves that limitation instead of claiming it is resolved.
concessions: The insurance claims triage segment misses target by 1.5 percentage points.
That segment is named in two carrier pilot commitments, so the limitation is potentially material under the policy text.
The product note calling the segment non-core does not resolve materiality on this record.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open.
There is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance or a final legal determination resolving the disclosure question.
